headline: Deep learning extends variant, regulatory and chromatin interaction prediction
label: Deep Learning Genomic Regulation Models
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair sequence-based deep models with orthogonal evidence such as MPRA, Hi-C and ChIP-seq to refine genomic predictions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the augmentation of sequence-based prediction with orthogonal molecular evidence. MPRabc combines MPRA-predicted reporter activity, sequence features, epigenomic signals and 3D contacts to improve enhancer-gene prediction, while SCEG-HiC uses bulk Hi-C as a prior for single-cell enhancer-gene links and GraphChIAr augments Hi-C maps with ChIP-seq profiles. MOSAIC fuses a DNA language model, multi-scale CNN and annotation features for noncanonical splice-altering variants, and Porcine MutBERT introduces SNP-targeted masking in lightweight genomic foundation models. A multi-species benchmark of ten splicing predictors reports AUROC losses of roughly 21 to 33 percent for task-specific and foundation models. Other items extend this pattern to causal network inference grounded in molecular evidence, base-resolution INDEL mutation rate maps, and long-read structural variant calling. What is new is the explicit integration of heterogeneous experimental layers rather than sequence alone.
